package_info.why_malicious: This package was created to impersonate the legitimate 'localforage-memoryStorageDriver' by using a lowercase-only variant of the name, exploiting a gap in NPM's package name policy. The intent was to deceive users into installing a malicious or placeholder package instead of the legitimate one, a form of typosquatting.

execution_context.file_location: package.json / index.js (implied, not shown in report)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Not explicitly shown in the report. The package was described as containing malicious code and was removed by the NPM security team.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the code would execute arbitrary JavaScript with the potential to access the filesystem or exfiltrate data, depending on the attacker's payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The package name is nearly identical to a popular legitimate package, differing only in capitalization, and was flagged and removed for containing malicious code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not impersonate other packages or contain code that executes on install with the intent to deceive or harm users.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may use similar names for forks or related projects, but not for the purpose of deception.
key_indicators: Package name mimics a popular package with only capitalization differences
Flagged and removed by NPM security team for malicious content
No legitimate project or documentation associated with the package

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a package with a name nearly identical to a popular package, differing only in capitalization.
attack_chain.leads_to: Users are tricked into installing the malicious package instead of the legitimate one.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes at install-time, potentially exfiltrating data or performing other harmful actions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of user systems or data.

behavioral_signatures: Package names that differ from popular packages only by capitalization
Unexpected install-time code execution in packages with no legitimate project history
Packages rapidly removed or flagged by NPM security team
file_indicators: package.json with suspiciously similar names to popular packages
index.js or main entry file containing obfuscated or unexpected install-time scripts
network_indicators: Outbound network requests during install-time from packages with suspicious names
Connections to domains not associated with the legitimate project
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new package uploads whose names differ from existing popular packages only by capitalization. Flag packages that execute code at install-time and have no legitimate project history or documentation. Use threat intelligence feeds to identify packages removed or flagged by the NPM security team. Employ static and dynamic analysis to detect unexpected network or filesystem activity during installation.
